title: Canalization Before Generalization: Grokking as a Dynamical Probe
hook: Nudge weight decay briefly during grokking's plateau and you shift when generalization arrives. Early nudges scatter; later ones line up by dose — a hidden selection finishing unseen.
key_points: Grokking separates fitting the training data from visible generalization, opening a window to study which solution gets selected.
Method: sweep short, fixed-duration weight-decay pulses across the plateau and measure how each shifts later generalization time.
Early pulses produce unordered shifts; later pulses produce a stable dose ordering across all three tasks tested.
Stronger weight-decay increases pull generalization earlier; stronger decreases push it later.
The ordering emerges before visible generalization — the selection is settled before the test-accuracy jump.
Test-loss barriers between perturbed and baseline checkpoints collapse toward zero while the timing effects persist.
content_html: For an overparameterized network, many solutions fit the training data equally well and behave completely differently on unseen data. Something during training picks one. Grokking — where test accuracy jumps long after training accuracy saturates — gives you a plateau to watch that picking happen in.
extra_html:
The probe

Lin sweeps short, fixed-duration weight-decay pulses across the grokking plateau and measures how each pulse shifts the time at which generalization later appears. Across three grokking tasks the pattern is consistent: pulses applied early in the plateau produce unordered shifts, but pulses applied later produce a stable dose ordering — stronger weight-decay increases lead to earlier generalization, stronger decreases to later. Crucially, this ordering emerges before visible generalization in all three tasks, so whatever it reflects has already settled by the time the test-accuracy jump shows up.

Canalization

Meanwhile a second measurement moves the other way: test-loss barriers between the perturbed and baseline generalization checkpoints collapse toward zero, indicating the reachable solutions are converging on one region. Lin names this combination — increasingly constrained solution selection alongside persistent dose-ordered timing sensitivity — the canalization of function selection, borrowing a term from developmental biology for a trajectory that becomes progressively channeled. The practical read: the plateau isn't idle, and regularization applied during it acts on when a mostly-decided solution surfaces rather than on which one you get. arXiv, 2026.

related.title: Grokking: Generalization Long After Overfitting
related.hook: A network memorizes the training set and seems done. Keep training anyway, and much later it can suddenly snap into real generalization — an effect called grokking.

related.title: Deep Double Descent
related.hook: Bigger models should overfit, then get worse — right? Instead test error often dips, climbs, then dips again as model size grows, breaking the classic bias-variance story.

related.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
related.hook: You can prune over 90% of a trained network and keep its accuracy. The catch: a tiny 'winning ticket' subnetwork was hiding inside the dense one from the start.

related.title: Overfitting & Regularization
related.hook: A model that aces its training data but flops on anything new hasn't learned — it has memorized. Regularization is the cure.

flashcards.prompt: What does the paper mean by 'canalization of function selection'?
flashcards.back_html: The combination of two things seen during grokking's plateau: solution selection becoming increasingly constrained (test-loss barriers collapsing toward zero) while timing stays sensitive to weight-decay dose in a stable order.

flashcards.prompt: What happens when a weight-decay pulse is applied early in the grokking plateau versus late?

choices.text: Early pulses shift generalization time unpredictably; later pulses produce a stable dose ordering
Early pulses always delay generalization; later pulses always advance it
Neither has any measurable effect on when generalization appears

flashcards.explanation_html: Across three grokking tasks the shifts are unordered early in the plateau but later settle into a stable ordering — stronger weight-decay increases generalize earlier, stronger decreases later.

flashcards.prompt: Why is grokking a useful probe for studying generalization?
flashcards.back_html: Because it pulls training fit and visible generalization apart in time, giving you a plateau during which you can intervene and watch how the network's choice among many training-fitting solutions gets narrowed.
